transcript.text: Is it normal for my dishwasher to leave everything wet? Plastic tubs are soaking every time and there's drips on the glasses. It's a Bosch Serie 4.

Some wetness is normal, particularly for plastic tubs: they do not retain heat, so condensation drying leaves droplets behind. Drips on glasses can also happen, but if everything is very wet it is usually rinse aid, an Eco/Quick programme with modest drying, or—only if the load is cold—a heating issue. With the dishwasher switched off, check the rinse-aid reservoir beside the detergent dispenser, top it up if needed and make sure its setting is not at minimum. At the end of the next normal or hotter programme, are the glasses and plates hot and steamy, or cold?
The rinse aid symbol is lit, so it's empty. I use all-in-one tablets. And yes, it's hot and steamy inside at the end of the cycle. I use Eco 50 every time.

The hot, steamy finish makes a heating fault unlikely. All-in-one tablets do not reliably replace rinse aid for drying, and an empty rinse-aid reservoir is very likely to be the main reason for drips on the glasses. Fill the reservoir with dishwasher rinse aid; leave its setting around the normal/middle range rather than minimum. Eco 50 uses condensation drying, so some water on plastic tubs is normal even when the machine is working properly—opening the door slightly once the programme has finished can help it escape as steam. If glasses and china remain very wet after rinse aid has been used for a cycle or two, try a hotter/non-Eco programme once; that separates normal Eco drying from a drying-system issue.

candidates: Normal condensation drying, especially on plastic items (high)
Low rinse aid or low rinse-aid setting (medium)
Programme with limited drying or a heating fault if the load is cold (low)
